question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{2}+4.$ For which of the following values of $k$ does the intermediate value theorem guarantee that $f(x)=k$ has a solution on the interval $x\in [2,5]?$
question.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[2,5],$ so the intermediate value theorem guarantees that $f(x)=k$ has a solution for each value of $k$ between $f(2)$ and $f(5).$

Since $f(2)=8$ and $f(5)=29,$ we must have 
$k\in [8,29].$

Among the given options, only $k=10$ belongs to the interval $[8,29].$
